subject: AWS private offer: billing handoff, approval windows & seniority checkpoints
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Hunt <sarah.hunt@fastpay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS private offer: initial billing handoff questions

Sarah —

Thanks for the time earlier. Following up with the private offer details so you can run this past your procurement and finance teams. A few items we need clarity on from FastPay to finalize the MPO: 

- Buyer approval path: who signs (CFO, Head of Procurement) and any delegations for pilot-sized PO (< $50k).
- Billing expectations: monthly invoice vs. upfront annual prepay for the 12-month term we discussed.
- Any contractual gating (security/insurance) that will add sign-off layers.

I've attached a pricing worksheet (workup) that shows both annual prepay and monthly invoice lines so you can see the cash-flow impact. If procurement prefers monthly invoicing we can route activation through the marketplace subscription flow rather than an upfront commitment, but that will change the discount profile.

Next step: can you confirm internal approvers and whether FastPay requires a PO number before activation? If procurement wants, we can loop in AWS partner sales to accelerate buyer approvals.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MPO_Pricing_Workup_v3.xlsx
From: Sarah Hunt <sarah.hunt@fastpay.com>

Cc: FastPay Procurement <procurement@fastpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer: initial billing handoff questions

Hi Marcus —

Appreciate the summary. Quick answers from procurement: 

- Signature: CFO signs anything > $100k. For the pilot (targeting $30k), the Head of Procurement (procurement@fastpay.com) can approve, but they will still require a PO for reconciliation.
- Billing: Finance prefers monthly invoicing for vendors where possible, but they are open to upfront annual payment if there is a meaningful discount and a clear refund/termination clause.
- Insurance & Security: Security asked for a short questionnaire but no additional signoffs beyond our standard SOC 2 attestation. I can pull that into the thread if helpful.

Important: procurement needs to see the marketplace billing routing — specifically whether AWS will invoice or Redwood will. That determines our internal AR process.

Can we get a clear mapping of: MPO created by Redwood -> who issues invoice (AWS vs Redwood) -> how FastPay receives PO/invoice?

Thanks,
Sarah
Senior Ops Manager, FastPay
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Hunt <sarah.hunt@fastpay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer: initial billing handoff questions

Sarah —

Summary below to make it explicit for procurement and finance. Apologies for the long message, but wanted to be precise on routing options: 

Option A — AWS-billed MPO (recommended for buyer AR simplicity)
- MPO is created in AWS Marketplace as a Private Offer tied to your AWS account.
- AWS issues the invoice to FastPay and handles collection; Redwood receives payout via marketplace settlement.
- FastPay receives an AWS invoice (PO applied) — internal AP team likes this because it flows to existing reconciliation.
- Discount profile: smaller seller-discount compared to direct billing; activation is immediate once MPO accepted.

Option B — Redwood-billed agreement with marketplace activation
- Contract and payment are managed directly with Redwood (we issue the invoice).
- We can offer a slightly deeper discount for annual prepay but FastPay AR would need to add a new vendor to the AP system.
- This path enables custom termination/refund clauses that some legal teams prefer.

Operational notes:
- For pilot <$50k, if FastPay prefers AWS billing, we can draft the MPO and request AWS partner sales to shepherd the acceptance so procurement sees the AWS invoice flow.
- If procurement needs a PO before activation, AWS can accept a PO number on the MPO acceptance step — that should be visible in the invoice metadata.

I've attached the updated mutual action plan that maps approvers and timelines (FastPay_Mutual_Action_Plan.docx).

Suggested next step: loop in AWS co-sell contact (Tom Liu) to confirm MPO creation and AWS invoicing cadence. Vanessa — can you please reach out to Tom to get his availability?

Best,
Marcus

Tom —

Looping you in to confirm the MPO routing for FastPay (deal DL-2026-0927-FP). FastPay procurement prefers AWS-issued invoices; they want to make sure acceptance on the MPO will generate an AWS invoice that goes to procurement@fastpay.com and includes the PO number field.

Can you confirm: 
- Whether AWS will issue invoices for private offers created by a partner listing (Redwood) and the cadence (monthly/one-off).
- If invoice metadata allows a PO number and department code so their AP team can auto-match.
- Any steps we should follow to ensure the MPO is listed with the correct seller ID so FastPay is billed by AWS (not Redwood directly).

Tom — Sarah is on this thread for procurement context. Karthik / I can share the MPO draft once we have confirmation from AWS on invoice behavior.

Redwood Inference
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@aws-partners.com>

Date: 2026-11-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS MPO routing & billing — request to confirm invoicing actor

Thanks for the ping and context. Confirming the following from AWS Marketplace side: 

- AWS can invoice buyers for Private Offers created by the seller partner. When the MPO is accepted under the buyer's AWS account, AWS issues the invoice to the buyer.
- Invoice cadence: AWS can issue a single invoice for upfront annual charges or monthly invoices for subscription-style billing — we support both, but the MPO must be configured accordingly at creation.
- PO metadata: AWS invoices support an embedded PO number field; buyers can include department codes in the invoice metadata for automated matching. Be sure to add the PO field on the MPO acceptance step.
- Seller ID: To make sure AWS bills FastPay (not Redwood directly), Redwood should create the MPO under the Redwood seller profile but mark the payout and billing routing as AWS-issued to the buyer. I can validate the seller ID and MPO payload before submission.

Action items: 
- Marcus/Karthik: please share the MPO draft (JSON or summary) and the pricing worksheet.
- Sarah/procurement: confirm the PO number format and whether AP needs any specific invoice line-items for GL mapping.
- Tom: please confirm a short validation call tomorrow morning so we can finalize MPO creation by EOD.

I'll set a 30-minute slot — sending invite.

Best,
Tom Liu
AWS Partner Solutions, Marketplace Enablement
